headline: Nations League: England shock Spain 3-2 in Madrid thriller to claim Group A3 top seed
teaser: Captain Harry Kane, Ezri Konsa, and Ben White strike as England build a 3-0 lead, surviving a spirited Spanish fightback and an Elliot Anderson red card to snap La Roja's 43-match unbeaten run.
story:
England produced one of their most remarkable away performances in recent memory on Sunday, 15 November, defeating European champions Spain 3-2 at the Riyadh Air Metropolitano in Madrid to clinch first place in UEFA Nations League Group A3.

Thomas Tuchel's side stunned the 63,788 crowd by opening the scoring on the stroke of halftime, when captain Harry Kane converted a 45th-minute penalty for his 73rd international goal. The Three Lions doubled their advantage eight minutes after the restart as Ezri Konsa headed home from a corner, before Ben White swept home a third on 58 minutes following a swift counter-attack.

Spain mounted a relentless fightback, with Mikel Oyarzabal converting a 65th-minute spot-kick and Nico Williams finishing neatly on 75 minutes. England were reduced to ten men when midfielder Elliot Anderson received a straight red card for a rash tackle in the 84th minute, but Jordan Pickford and a resolute backline withstood intense pressure through seven minutes of stoppage time to snap Spain's 43-match unbeaten competitive streak dating back to March 2023.
whyCareReason: England snap Spain's 43-match competitive unbeaten streak in Madrid, leapfrogging the European champions to take the seeded quarter-final berth in Nations League Group A3.
stakes: England claim top seed in Group A3 for the two-legged quarter-finals in March 2027, while Spain advance as unseeded runners-up.
rivalryAngle: Sweet redemption for England after falling 2-1 to Spain in the Euro 2024 final in Berlin, earning their first victory on Spanish soil in eight years.
funFacts: Harry Kane scored his 73rd international goal on his 126th cap, converting a penalty on 45 minutes.
Spain's loss was their first defeat in a competitive fixture in 43 matches dating back to March 2023.
England built a 3-0 lead inside 58 minutes through Kane, Konsa, and White before holding on with ten men.
